html:
The Battle of White Mountain was fought on 8 November 1620 just west of Prague, where Catholic armies of the emperor Ferdinand II crushed the army of the Bohemian Protestant estates in about two hours.

The rebel king Frederick V fled and was mocked as the Winter King. In 1621 twenty seven leaders of the revolt were executed in Prague's Old Town Square. Protestant nobles lost their lands, which went to Catholic and foreign families, and Protestants were forced to convert or leave; tens of thousands emigrated, including Comenius. German became the language of rule. Czech nationalists later called the next era the darkness. The battle was an early stage of the Thirty Years' War and tied Bohemia to the Habsburgs until 1918.
sum: The Battle of White Mountain was fought on 8 November 1620 just west of Prague, where Catholic armies of the emperor Ferdinand II crushed the army of the Bohemian Protestant estates in about two hours.
